clinician.final_diagnosis: Primary cardiac lymphoma (PCL) with cerebral relapse as recurrent diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)
clinician.trajectory_summary: In 2007, a 37-year-old man presented with haemodynamic cardiac compromise. Chest MRI showed a large right heart mass invading the right atrium and mediastinum. Although histopathology of the cardiac biopsy is not documented, the cardiac tumour immunophenotype is described as similar to the later brain biopsy. In 2012, a brain biopsy revealed recurrent DLBCL (CD10, CD19, CD20 positive), confirming cerebral relapse of the previously suspected primary cardiac lymphoma. Post-2012, the patient was successfully treated with high-dose methotrexate leading to disappearance of the brain mass. Subsequent follow-ups noted persistent neurological symptoms with gradual cognitive improvement but no evidence of tumor recurrence as late as 2017.
